rows.headline: EU faces winter gas shortage and potential demand cuts after Hormuz crisis
rows.hook: Trapped LNG supply triggers European gas shortfall
rows.summary: The European Union enters winter with historically low natural gas storage levels, which may force a 7 percent cut in energy demand. A report by the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis attributes the tight market to conflict in Iran that has trapped a fifth of global liquefied natural gas behind the Strait of Hormuz. European natural gas prices have surged significantly since early March as a result. Indian retail investors should monitor this situation because European energy crunches can push global LNG prices higher, driving up domestic gas and fertilizer costs.
